challenges.name: provider-scopes-quiz
challenges.title: One instance or many? Read the logs
challenges.description: A singleton that held the current learner, a request-scoped provider deep in the injection chain, and a shutdown hook that never ran. Decide whether each statement is True or False.

questions.explanation: False. Node.js runs JavaScript on one thread, but every await hands control back to the event loop, which runs other requests' code in between. A default-scope provider is a single instance shared by every request, so while req-a was waiting for findById, req-b's guard overwrote ctx.userId, and req-a then saved lesson 3 for learner u_42. The misconception is that "single-threaded" means "one request at a time": requests interleave at every await. Per-request data belongs in the method arguments, in AsyncLocalStorage, or in a request-scoped provider - never in a field of a singleton.

False. Request scope bubbles up the injection chain: ProgressService depends on a request-scoped provider, so Nest has to create a new ProgressService for every request to give it that request's RequestContext, and the same happens to ProgressController. The log shows the line once per request - three times - and not at startup. ProgressRepository is not affected, because it does not depend on anything request-scoped. The misconception is that the scope you write in @Injectable() is the scope you get; it is the narrowest scope among the provider and everything it depends on.

True. Shutdown hooks (onModuleDestroy, beforeApplicationShutdown, onApplicationShutdown) are disabled by default because listening for signals has a cost. Without app.enableShutdownHooks(), SIGTERM ends the process with Node's default behaviour - exit code 143 is 128 + 15, killed by SIGTERM - and no hook runs. With it, Nest calls the hooks before the process exits, and the log line would show (SIGTERM). The misconception is that implementing OnApplicationShutdown is enough on its own; onModuleInit and onApplicationBootstrap run without extra setup, the shutdown hooks do not.
